headline: Sunday evening's cold front is now in the models: RRFS shows a 0.36 in burst around 5 to 8 PM Sunday, but ECMWF, NBM and GFS keep the wettest 3 hours near 0.1 in, so the rating card stays at none; dry through Saturday, channel at base flow.

summary.text: Sunday's front has entered the window. RRFS wettest 3 hours rose from 0.04 to 0.36 in; NBM storm total from 0.08 to 0.29 in, ECMWF from 0.20 to 0.31 in.
Wettest 3 hours: RRFS 0.36, ECMWF 0.11, NBM 0.09, GFS 0.09 in. RRFS is the outlier. HRRR (zero rain) only reaches 10 AM Sunday, before the front.
Rating card consensus about 0.09 in (middle of HRRR 0, NBM 0.09, RRFS 0.36): none. Even RRFS is about half of the 0.71 in Yellow (garage) line.
Dry through Saturday night. Light rain from Sunday midday; heaviest most likely about 5 to 8 PM Sunday. RRFS shows a smaller second cell around 2 to 3 AM Monday.
Burst falls on an outgoing tide: 7.9 ft high at 3:33 PM Sunday, low at 10:43 PM. Surge runs 1.3 to 1.5 ft. Channel at Alameda 0.12 ft, far below Monitoring 3.18 ft.
Clear street drain grates and yard drains of leaves Saturday. No need to move cars. Avoid the Bay shore around midday high tides through Sunday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text:
High pressure keeps Friday and Saturday dry and unusually warm, highs upper 60s to low 70s, with Saturday the warmer day (NWS San Francisco). The storm door reopens Sunday: a cold front brings cooler air, gusts of 25 to 35 mph, and rain Sunday into Monday. In its overnight long-term discussion (12:41 AM Friday) NWS calls this a weak system with largely beneficial rain, up to 0.25 in for most of the Bay Area, 0.25 to 0.5 in in the Santa Cruz Mountains and 0.25 to 0.75 in in the North Bay. That is softer wording than Thursday afternoon's "moderate, briefly heavy" and no newer long-term update was in this snapshot.

A second low Tuesday into Wednesday, now expected to track toward Southern California, could bring 0.25 to 0.75 in to the Bay Area (less if it tracks farther south, more if it shifts north); it is mostly beyond this 72-hour window.

sections.title: Model trends
sections.text:
From 1 PM Friday to 1 PM Monday, wettest 3 hours / storm total:
• RRFS (4 AM run): 0.36 / 0.57 in, about 5 to 8 PM Sunday; biggest hour 0.13 in. Up from 0.04 / 0.05 in yesterday.
• ECMWF: 0.11 / 0.31 in, about 4 to 7 PM Sunday (was 0.09 / 0.20).
• NBM: 0.09 / 0.29 in, steady light rain about 4 to 10 PM Sunday (was 0.05 / 0.08).
• GFS: 0.09 / 0.13 in, about 5 to 8 PM Sunday (was 0.01 / 0.01).
• HRRR hourly (11 AM run, back after missing yesterday): 0.00 in through 10 AM Sunday, its last hour.
• HRRR 15-minute (through 11:45 PM Saturday): 0.00 in.

What changed: yesterday the front sat just past the end of the model window; now every model brings rain Sunday evening, and all agree on the timing within about an hour. They disagree on intensity. RRFS concentrates the rain into a three-hour band with hourly rates of 0.10 to 0.13 in, while the global models and NBM spread a similar or smaller total over six or more hours at about 0.03 to 0.04 in per hour. RRFS has a habit of over-intensifying convective bands, and this is an older run, so the consensus near 0.1 in is a reasonable middle. HRRR will start covering Sunday evening in the next several runs; it is the model to watch, keeping in mind it has under-forecast big local bursts by about 3 times. No model reaches a 1-hour rate of 0.40 in, the automatic Yellow trigger.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 7 AM Sunday) is now running 1.3 to 1.5 ft above predicted highs at Redwood City, a bit more than yesterday's 0.8 to 1.1 ft. Today's 9.1 ft high at 1:28 PM was modeled near 10.4 ft around 1:50 PM. Saturday: 7.1 ft at 3:56 AM (about 8.5 ft) and 8.6 ft at 2:27 PM (about 9.9 ft). Sunday: 7.2 ft at 4:49 AM (about 8.7 ft), then 7.9 ft at 3:33 PM, beyond the model run.

The Sunday burst lines up well for drainage: it arrives after the 3:33 PM high on a falling tide headed to a -0.4 ft low at 10:43 PM. RRFS's smaller 2 to 3 AM Monday cell comes on the rising tide ahead of a 7.4 ft high at 5:42 AM.

NWS Coastal Flood Advisory (1:31 AM) for Bayshore locations until 5 PM Sunday: up to 1.7 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, with San Francisco high tides 1.7 ft above normal Friday, 1.6 ft Saturday and 0.9 ft Sunday, including up to 1.3 ft of surge. This affects the Bay shore and tidal sloughs, not Athlone Terrace directly.

Channel at Alameda de las Pulgas: 0.12 ft at 1 PM, flat between 0.11 and 0.13 ft for the past day (Monitoring 3.18 ft, Watch 4.6 ft, Warning 5.65 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at its latest report, 5:13 AM today (Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry and warm. The Caltrain rain gauge showed no rain in the 24 hours to its 5:13 AM report and is still reporting only about every 12 hours. The hourly Alameda channel gauge is steady at base flow.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Timing is fairly well agreed (Sunday late afternoon and evening); intensity is not. If RRFS's banded scenario verifies, the street sees a short period of heavy rain, still about half of what has brought water to the garage doors in past storms. If the global models are right, it is a steady soaking with no street impact. A thunderstorm cell is the wild card, but NWS keeps the under-20 % thunder chance in the North Bay. The next HRRR runs, which will reach Sunday evening by Saturday afternoon, should narrow this.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Saturday (dry and warm): clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, and check sandbags and flashlights ahead of Sunday's front and the Tuesday system.
• No need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac at this point.
• Sunday evening: keep this page open around 5 to 8 PM; if rain turns heavy, timestamped photos of the street help calibrate the rating.
• Stay off the Bay shore, piers and low shoreline roads around the midday high tides through Sunday, and don't walk or drive through moving water.
